description: The sea's life's calls by day, each from a group there, perMinute a minute from each group, heard within reach metres and kept quiet beside the wind and the sea. The laughing gull's laugh: a run of short, nasal notes, 'ha-ha-ha-ha', a harmonic voice its band near 1.1 to 1.6 kHz, falling at its end (the Cornell Lab's All About Birds: 'a raucous, laughing ha-ha-ha'); a note lasts note seconds, notes notes a call, gap seconds apart, each falling to fall of its pitch, the band's sharpness q. The sooty tern's 'ker-wacki-wah' or 'wide-awake': three nasal syllables, higher and harsher than a gannet's rasp, near 2 to 2.8 kHz, the last the longest and falling (BirdLife International; Audubon's Guide to North American Birds); each syllable lasts its syllables' seconds, gap apart. The brown booby's whistle: the male's thin, high whistle, short, rising a little at its end (Cornell Lab's Birds of the World), as a colony's boobies whistle. Frequencies in Hz, times in seconds, levels as gains.
